notes: Zhaobaogou culture of the Luan River valley; the page gives '(5400-4500 BC)', 'found primarily in the Luan River valley in Inner Mongolia and northern Hebei', type site 'discovered in Aohan Banner, Chifeng, Inner Mongolia' and 'excavated in 1986'. The infobox of the Zhaobaogou page has no dates, no predecessor and no successor, and the text does not mention the Xinglongwa, Xinle or Hongshan; the relations come from the other pages: Xinglongwa infobox 'Followed by: Zhaobaogou culture'; Hongshan infobox 'Preceded by: Xinglongwa culture, Xinle culture, Zhaobaogou culture' and 'The Zhaobaogou culture may be contemporary with Xinle and a little later'. Overlap: the Zhaobaogou page runs to 4500 BC but the Hongshan page begins at 4700; from 4700 the Chifeng part and the cells shared with the Hongshan discs pass to the Hongshan (confidence 1, the pages are silent on any hand-over; a 2025 study cited on the Hongshan page links 'the earlier local Zhaobaogou culture' to Hongshan ancestry) and the Chengde part is drawn to 4500, after which it is nobody's land (no follower on any page). Extent: Chifeng 100 km + Chengde 100 km are placements for 'Luan River valley' and Aohan (the gazetteer has no Luan River). No area figure.
